facts.fact: The interior ministry's own policy of January 2021 states that the civil registration system has collapsed, that no civil registration services have been launched by the government and that there is no central registry or tracking of the certificates that ministries, courts and federal member states issue independently.
facts.system: CRVS system (to be created under the policy)

facts.fact: At January 2021 the policy records no government civil registration service in operation; installing ICT equipment in selected maternal and child health centres and municipal civil registrar departments, and training system users in selected districts, are listed as priority actions still to be done.
facts.system: CRVS system (to be created under the policy)

facts.fact: The policy makes the Ministry of Interior, Federal Affairs and Reconciliation responsible for the policy's goals and for running civil registration at federal, district, municipal and village level, with municipalities registering and issuing certificates and the ministry's Civil Registration Unit as secretariat of the technical working group.
facts.system: CRVS system (to be created under the policy)

facts.fact: The National CRVS Policy of January 2021 sets priorities to 2025, among them designing and building an automated system for electronic capture, processing, storage and retrieval of CRVS information with a national central database, starting with a pilot phase.
facts.system: CRVS system (to be created under the policy)

facts.fact: The policy names no budget line: it says the government will cultivate partnerships with stakeholders and donors to obtain the necessary funds and that phase 1 is contingent on engagement with bilateral and multilateral partners.
facts.system: CRVS system (to be created under the policy)
